lesson_title: The Only Continent in All Four Halves
hook_text: Cut the Earth in half twice. Only one continent gets sliced by both knives, and you are standing on it.
clip_script: Cut the Earth like an orange around the middle: that is the equator, splitting the Northern Hemisphere from the Southern. Cut it again from pole to pole, along the prime meridian through Greenwich and back up the far side along the hundred and eightieth line: that splits east from west. Four halves, and every place lives in two of them. Johannesburg is south and east. London is north and, just barely, west. Now look at which continent both knives cut. The equator slices through Kenya and the Congo. The prime meridian slices through Ghana. Africa is the only continent in all four hemispheres. And here is a surprise: most of Africa is actually north of the equator, because it is so wide at the top. One more thing. Same day, opposite seasons. When London shivers at Christmas, Durban goes to the beach.
visual_style: A whiteboard globe sliced by two glowing lines; Africa lights up in four colours where the lines cross it; a split screen of a snowy London and a sunny Durban beach on the same calendar date.
mood: Playful surprise and a little African pride.
pacing: Two quick cuts, a reveal of Africa, then the seasonal twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and place any country in its hemispheres.
